The decisive flaw is the verification command: it asserts the fragments 'field-changing' and 'A-REVISION-LOOP' are present in .research/auto_research.json after apply, yet the node statement in patch_preview contains neither — it uses 'field changes' (unhyphenated) and never mentions 'A-REVISION-LOOP'. Post-apply verification therefore cannot exit 0; the command tests strings the patch never writes, so this proposal would verify-fail on its own terms and stall the loop. Per the very contract it records, a corrected proposal must come back from A with the node statement literally containing the asserted fragments, or with the verification fragments dropped. The recorded content itself is faithful to the launch protocol and semantically novel (nothing prior records the critic revision contract), so the idea is worth keeping — the fragment mismatch, not the patch, is the closure risk.

detail.reason: Patch op: add_edge is acceptable but the claim 'no file-write risk' overstates — it mutates .research/auto_research.json through the pipeline, which is fine, but say so honestly. Verification command: exit-0 is right, yet the assertion checks only from/to and never e.get('kind')=='dependency'; a wrong-kind edge between the same endpoints would pass, so strengthen the python check to assert kind. It also asserts presence but not that no other edges changed; that is only partially covered by the unittest suite, so state explicitly that the suite validates graph schema/acyclicity. Dependency-closure risk: the real gap is a cycle — if VERIFY-DRY-RUN's existing closure (P-175 exercised both nodes) already contains B-VERIFY-RECORD, this edge creates a cycle that could break graph validation; the proposal asserts direction is hard-checked but does not show the cycle case is covered. If the suite lacks an acyclicity test, a future exit-0 could still pass with an invalid graph. Ask A for a corrected proposal adding the kind check to the assertion and confirming the suite's graph-validation coverage before I verify.

The patch op is nominally local, but the case is not closed on three grounds. (1) Verification command is too weak: it asserts the substring 'must name at least one concrete defect' appears anywhere in .research/auto_research.json and that the file parses; it never navigates the JSON to prove B-CRITIC-SPECIFICITY's statement was actually updated, never checks the node exists, and never runs the harness's own validator/schema check. Exit-0 can pass while the set_node_statement op silently no-oped or wrote into a different record. A corrected command must load the JSON, walk to the node, assert its statement equals the new text, and then run the pipeline's validation. (2) Dependency-closure risk is asserted nil, not verified: the proposal does not demonstrate that B-CRITIC-SPECIFICITY has no dependents whose statements reference it, and does not confirm set_node_statement is an op revise/apply actually supports; if the op type is unsupported, the patch is unappliable and should be resubmitted. (3) Inert-state risk the proposal itself flags: nothing in the harness consumes this statement text, so absent evidence that a reader (launch prompt, critic skill, or validator) enforces the node's content, this repeats the P-173/P-174/P-176 weak-effect bookkeeping pattern it claims to fix — the contract is not machine-checkable by this verification. The narrative about the rejection streak is not evidence. Resubmit with a node-level verification command, evidence of op support and a clean dep closure, and a statement of which consumer enforces the contract, or I will reject on inert-state grounds.

set_launch_prompt is reversible and correctly scoped, but the verification command is vacuous: it asserts the substring MECH-DIFF exists anywhere in auto_research.json, and the proposal record itself (title, statement, patch_preview) contains that string, so exit-0 passes even if role A's prompt was never changed or the rule landed on the wrong role — a false-positive verification that could trust an unapplied patch and decay trust further. Fix: parse the JSON, load the actual role-A prompt list, and assert the MECH-DIFF bullet is present in that exact field. Second, the mechanical claim is overstated: this is still a soft in-context instruction A must self-enforce — the same memory that failed across P-173/P-174/P-176/P-177 — so it may not operationalize anything; a hard gate in tooling that rejects candidates whose op-family plus invariant matches a Recent proposals entry would be the real mechanism. Third, the falsifier is weak: five proposals with no repeat can pass by chance without ever exercising the rule; require a directed probe (re-offer the P-173 family under fresh wording and check the prompt blocks or forces divergence) or extend the window. If the verification command is corrected to check the actual role-A prompt content and the mechanism claim is narrowed accordingly, I will pass.

Intent is sound (title-renaming duplicates escape A-CHECK), and the single set_node_statement op on A-CHECK keeps blast radius small with M0 and B untouched. But three problems. (1) Verification is a string-containment check, not a hard check: 'python3 -c ... assert "A-CHECK" in t' passes if those substrings exist anywhere in the file — e.g., in the old statement, B critiques, or the patch_preview itself — without proving the A-CHECK node's statement actually equals the proposed text. It never parses the node, so a failed apply (or an applied-but-truncated statement) still exits 0. (2) Closure risk: this edits the statement only; if tools/auto_research.py contains any duplicate-title or equivalence enforcement, the code and the contract now diverge and the invariant stays unenforced — a documentation change masquerading as a behavior change. The proposal should state explicitly whether enforcement code exists and patch it, or prove none exists. (3) The falsifier is circular/soft: equivalence is 'same invariant+ops+intended effect', but 'intended effect' is itself judged ad hoc by the same A/B judgment the rule was meant to constrain, and the only detection path is a future B critique — soft judgment, not the exit-0 hard verification the harness demands. Also 'open retrospectives count as equivalents' is a new policy buried in a statement rewrite; that should be a separate explicit change. Please revise with a verification that parses .research/auto_research.json, locates the A-CHECK node, and asserts its statement equals the patch preview exactly, plus a statement on whether enforcement code needs a matching patch.

detail.reason: Patch op is acceptable: single state-only set_node_statement on A-CHECK. Satisfiability check passes: 'unknown node id' and 'existing-graph list' appear verbatim in the patch statement (the third assertion, 'A-CHECK' in s, is pre-true since the node key already exists, so it adds no proof — minor). Two blockers before pass. (1) Dependency-closure risk: set_node_statement replaces the full statement text; P-184 claims complementarity with P-178/P-180/P-183 but does not show they avoid A-CHECK. If any of them also set_node_statement A-CHECK in this epoch, the applies are mutually destructive and ordering-dependent — one patch silently clobbers the others. A must confirm distinct targets or define merge semantics. (2) Enforcement gap: the guard is prose only; it 'mutates no state, changes no verification semantics,' meaning no pipeline code reads the launch prompt's existing-graph list. Unless that list is a defined, parseable artifact wired into A-CHECK's drafting path, the constraint is cosmetic and the falsification (B applying an unknown-id proposal) tests nothing the patch changed. State which code path consumes the list, or the revision is unfalsifiable and should be rejected. Both are expressible as a corrected proposal; resubmit.

Patch op is a single state-only set_node_statement, so the one-op rule is satisfied. Satisfiability check passes: the verification command asserts the substring 'already fully entailed by an existing node statement or launch-prompt rule', which the patch writes verbatim, so exit-0 is genuinely achievable. Closure risk: strengthening NOVELTY-GUARD's semantics may retroactively invalidate previously accepted proposals whose novelty was only paraphrase-level, and any nodes depending on NOVELTY-GUARD get deprecated by the change; the proposal names no revalidation step, so dependency closure is left broken after apply. Self-reference hazard: if NOVELTY-GUARD's current statement already entails this rule, P-186 is non-novel by its own criterion — ask A for the current node statement and a before/after diff showing the change is not merely cosmetic. Request a corrected proposal that includes the old-vs-new statement diff and an explicit revalidation plan for dependent nodes before I can pass.

Patch op set_node_statement on B-VERIFY-RECORD is state-only and acceptable, and the verification string is written verbatim, so satisfiability holds in principle. But three issues. (1) Locality/false-positive: the verifier greps the entire auto_research.json for 'recorded command does not match the executed command verbatim'; if that substring already exists anywhere (another node, logs, prior statement) the check exits 0 without the patch. It must target node B-VERIFY-RECORD's statement specifically, and A must demonstrate fail-before/pass-after on the actual epoch file. (2) Enforcement gap: the statement asserts runtime behavior — 'no apply may occur unless the record holds the exact command and exit 0; apply is blocked' — but the verifier only proves text presence, not that the engine enforces the gate. This is prose-only unless the code path implementing apply/verify reads and honors that record; verification should exercise that path (e.g., simulate a mismatch and assert apply is refused), not just grep JSON. (3) Dependency closure: B-VERIFY-RECORD gates apply; changing its statement deprecates dependents that check the old text, and no closure revalidation is proposed. Ask A to scope the verifier to the target node, add a mismatch-simulation enforcement check or explicitly scope the statement to documentation-only, and declare the dependency set before I pass.

Patch op is clean: single state-only add_node, and the marker N-VERIFY-DOUBLE-RUN-51e8 is written verbatim in the node statement, so the verification assertion is satisfiable and should fail-before/pass-after (unique marker suffix). The satisfiability check passes. The problem is dependency-closure risk: the safety premise 'no legitimate apply is blocked' rests entirely on P-189's read-only hermetic confinement, but the node's own statement does not reference or condition on P-189 being applied and validated. If P-189 is only drafted or was deprecated by a later apply, double-run verification will block legitimate proposals whose commands exit 0 once but create state on first run, or worse, reject already-applied nodes on revalidation. The proposal also overstates detection: double-run only catches commands whose exit code flips between runs; a state-mutating command that exits 0 twice still passes, so the invariant is weaker than the falsification evidence suggests. Request A to re-propose the node conditioned on P-189's applied/validated status (or explicitly scoped to commands already confined hermetic), then B must check ab-status for P-189 before any apply and hard-verify fail-before/pass-after on the corrected node.

The patch op is state-only (add_node) and the verification command asserts strings the patch writes verbatim ('N-TRUST-DECAY-DISTANCE', 'distance-aware'), failing pre-patch and passing post-patch — those gates are fine. But the node's own Safety text claims 'the rule changes only how decay is distributed', which add_node cannot do: the patch records text only, and nothing makes the engine consume this node type, so the asserted invariant is unenforceable unless the engine already implements distance-aware decay — in which case the proposal is a non-novel restatement of existing behavior (a negative example). The statement is also self-contradictory: it claims decay is 'currently flat across the closure' yet writes an invariant prescribing distance-aware decay as if it already held. The falsification evidence ('a 2-hop dependent decayed as much as its own 1-hop dependent') describes engine behavior that no code path in this patch touches. The verification command is minimal substring checking; it does not schema-validate the new node or check consistency with the existing decay mechanism. Ask A for a corrected proposal: state whether the engine currently applies flat or distance-aware decay, and either (a) rewrite the node as a purely descriptive assumption consistent with implemented behavior, or (b) include the engine change as a complete unified diff, plus a verification command that parses .research/auto_research.json and validates the node.

The single set_node_statement op is state-only, but the patch writes only a prose declaration; nothing in it or the verification enforces structural-delta checking, so a pure-paraphrase revision could still be accepted and the falsification clause stays unmechanized. The verification command is weakly scoped: it greps json.dumps of the whole document for 'A-REVISION-LOOP' (trivially true pre-patch) and a substring, rather than reading the node's statement field, so it cannot distinguish node text from prose elsewhere; rejected predecessors P-190/191/192 persisted in the same file could already contain the asserted phrase, making the command pass before the patch and breaking fail-before/pass-after. It also never fails on a wording-only revision, so it does not test the invariant it names. Scope the assert to node A-REVISION-LOOP's statement (e.g., diff-style or jsonpath), assert exact field text the patch writes verbatim, and confirm the command exits non-zero pre-patch before pass.

Non-novel restatement: the required content (invariant changed, why safe, falsifying evidence) is already imposed by the B launch prompt and by the kill-criterion rules in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, so this add_node encodes an existing gate rather than a new behavior. The patch is a single state-only add_node (fine), but N-FALSIFICATION-CONDITION is a draft L4 assumption with no enforcement wiring: nothing in the gate reads it, so B's behavior is unchanged. Verification command asserts only substrings the patch writes verbatim ('N-FALSIFICATION-CONDITION', 'explicit falsification condition') — satisfiable, but it only proves the text landed, not that proposals are actually rejected without it, so the claimed enforcement is unverified. Before pass, A must either show this node is not already implied by existing nodes/launch prompts, or wire it into the B gate so the verification can fail before the patch and pass after.

One state-only set_node_statement op on B-CRITIC-SPECIFICITY with no edge/status change is closure-safe, and the patch text does write 'concrete assertion' and 'satisfiability gap' verbatim, so the satisfiability check itself passes. But the verification command is not discriminative: asserting 'B-CRITIC-SPECIFICITY' in the JSON passes before the patch, because that node id already exists (this is an amendment, not a new node), so the command likely exits 0 pre-patch and cannot prove the patch applied. This violates the fail-before/pass-after requirement. Revise the command to assert a phrase unique to the new statement, e.g. 'must name the exact verification command' or 'is not specific and must be revised', which fails pre-patch and passes only after set_node_statement lands; optionally add a diff-based check on the node's statement field.

The patch writes the assertion string 'timeout' verbatim in the statement, so the text-match satisfiability check passes, and add_node is a single state-only op. But the proposal is self-inconsistent: its own verification_command has no explicit timeout wrapper, so under the very rule it adds, B would reject this proposal's command. Also the command only checks the literal word 'timeout' in the node text, not the enforced rejection behavior, and globbing paths[0] can pick a graph without the node and false-fail. Ask A to resubmit with the command wrapped in an explicit timeout (e.g. 'timeout 60 python3 ...') and to state that textual presence is the only verifiable target for an assumption node.

The single state-only set_node_statement is acceptable, but verification only greps for 'B-PATCH-HASH-RECORD-V1' in auto_research.json; it never tests that SHA-256 is stored or that mismatched hashes are rejected. It asserts a string the patch writes verbatim, so the satisfiability check is trivially true yet vacuous. Worse, the proposal changes only the B-VERIFY-RECORD statement, not any recording code or schema; existing applied-status entries carry no hash, so the new rule makes all current records non-compliant with no patch to add hash fields. That is an unclosed dependency: the mandate has no enforcing mechanism and would reject the very records it governs. Ask A to either add patch ops/code that actually persist and compare hashes, or reframe the node as a forward-only rule with an exit-0 verification that fails before and passes after while exercising the hash logic, not marker presence.

Patch op set_node_statement targets node B-REVALIDATE-GATE, but it is unconfirmed whether that node already exists in auto_research.json. If it is absent, set_node_statement may not create it, so the verification command (which asserts the statement text in auto_research.json) would either fail or pass against a pre-existing stale string rather than the applied patch. The satisfiability check between the two asserted strings and the written statement does hold verbatim, but the closure risk is unfalsifiable without confirming node existence and observing exit code fail-before/pass-after. Ask A to confirm the node exists or use a create-if-missing op, and require the verification command to fail before the patch and pass after.

P-202's add_node only inserts a declarative assumption; it writes no code enforcing a temp cwd or external-write detection, so the claimed hermetic hardening is unenforced. The verification greps for the sentinel B-VERIFY-HERMETIC-SENTINEL-7c1e and then checks the same file contains 'N-VERIFY-HERMETIC', which the patch writes verbatim; it therefore passes on text presence, not on behavior, yielding a self-referential exit-0 that hardens nothing. Before patch it fails (sentinel absent), so fail-before/pass-after is satisfied but vacuous. Ask A for a corrected proposal that either (1) provides a complete unified diff modifying runner verification code to mkdtemp, set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, and fail on writes outside the temp dir, with a verification that executes a canary write outside the dir and asserts failure, or (2) retargets the node as an explicit dependency on an implemented N-VERIFY-HERMETIC mechanism rather than an unfunded mandate.

The patch is declarative only: set_node_statement writes a rule description into NOVELTY-GUARD, and the verification command merely asserts that description string appears in auto_research.json. No actual automatic pre-verification lexical-uniqueness gate is implemented, so the title's mechanism is unverified—the check would pass on text presence alone. Also this restates existing launch-prompt negative-example guidance (challenge non-novel restatement) rather than adding novel machinery. Verbatim satisfiability holds (needle is a prefix substring of the patched statement), but before/after fail-then-pass behavior and any runtime enforcement remain unproven. Ask A to either provide an executable gate patch or narrow the claim to a documentation-only statement.
